Reading the STAR-minus-Score5 gap: a positive gap (the right-hand panel of each chart) means the runoff step is helping -- STAR resolves the primary's raw scores into a better outcome than just trusting the highest total. Zero or negative means the runoff is neutral or actively hurting relative to the raw scores it was fed.

Observed: at t=1.0/awareness_l=1.0/fatigue_l=1.0 (clean conditions), STAR edges out Score5 by +1.6 to +1.7 points -- the runoff earns its keep when it has genuine signal to work with. That edge shrinks and reverses as friction increases: STAR trails Score5 by roughly 2-6 points across most of the awareness_l and fatigue_l range (e.g. -5.9 pts at awareness_l=0.5, -5.0 pts at fatigue_l=0.0), though confidence intervals widen enough at the extremes (+/-15-17 pts) that the epistemic_t sweep alone doesn't cleanly separate STAR from Score5 in either direction. The clearer, higher-confidence story is in Section 21's per-election diagnostic below -- and even more starkly in Section 17's runoff_t sweep, where STAR's actual runoff_t=None behavior (41.6% VSE under Moderate friction) sits dramatically below what a delayed runoff at the SAME knowledge level would achieve (69.3% at t=0.70) -- a ~28-point gap that dwarfs the corresponding gap for AT2/PT3C/AT3C (each within ~1-3 points of their own runoff_t=None reference point), confirming STAR's runoff is uniquely exposed to corruption specifically because it reuses the primary's own ballots instead of treating the runoff as an independent decision.

21. Per-election "runoff betrayal" diagnostic¶

Section 20 measures the runoff's net effect in aggregate VSE. This section asks a more direct, mechanistic question: for the SPECIFIC pair of finalists STAR's runoff has to resolve in a given election, how often does the corrupted ballot data flip the pairwise decision away from what the SAME voters' true, uncorrupted utilities would have decided? A "betrayal" here means: the runoff, using the actual cast (noisy/friction-affected) ballots, picks one finalist over the other, but if the SAME voters had somehow expressed their true preferences instead, the runoff would have picked the OTHER one -- the corrupted signal didn't just add noise around the honest answer, it flipped the answer for this specific decision.

runoff_betrayal_stats below recomputes STAR's primary top-2 and the pairwise upset sign from the actual cast (noisy/friction-affected) ballots (mirroring Srv0to.results(), Section 1), then compares it against the SAME pairwise sign computed from HONEST ballots -- ballots cast the same way (same honBallot floor-to-0..topRank discretization, mirroring true_condorcet_winner's pairwise-sign primitive from Section 8, restricted to the one runoff pair) but on the TRUE, uncorrupted electorate, NOT the raw continuous true utilities directly. That distinction matters: honBallot's floor() alone is lossy even with zero noise -- a small honest margin between two candidates can floor to a tie while a larger one survives, which can flip the AGGREGATE pairwise sign on close pairs purely from STAR's coarse 0..5 ballot scale, before any noise is involved. Comparing against honest ballots in the same discretized format cancels that confound out, isolating exactly the marginal effect of epistemic_t/awareness_l/fatigue_l -- matching the "if honest scores were given" framing this diagnostic is meant to test. A finer-grained voter-level corruption rate is tracked the same way: among voters with a genuine (nonzero) honest preference for the pair, what fraction had their ACTUAL ballot's sign for that pair disagree -- the raw rate feeding the aggregate betrayal decision. Ballots are built directly (true electorate -> make_perceived_electorate -> apply_participation_friction -> honBallot, plus a parallel honest-only pass) rather than through resultsTable, since resultsTable's return shape doesn't expose the cast ballots and the true electorate together for the same election.

In [54]:
def runoff_betrayal_stats(topRank, niter, epistemic_t=1.0, awareness_l=1.0, fatigue_l=1.0,
                           electorates=None):
    """For niter STAR elections: recompute the primary top-2 as Srv0to.results() does using the
    ACTUAL cast (noisy/friction-affected) ballots, then compare the resulting pairwise upset sign
    against the upset sign from HONEST ballots cast the same way (same honBallot floor-to-
    0..topRank discretization) but on the TRUE, uncorrupted electorate -- NOT against the raw
    continuous true utilities directly. That distinction matters: honBallot's floor() alone
    (Section 1) is lossy even at epistemic_t=awareness_l=fatigue_l=1.0 -- small honest margins
    between two candidates can floor to a tie while larger ones survive, which can flip the
    AGGREGATE pairwise sign on close pairs purely from a coarse 0..5 ballot scale, with no noise
    involved at all. Comparing against honest ballots in the SAME discretized format cancels that
    confound out, isolating exactly the marginal effect of epistemic_t/awareness_l/fatigue_l --
    matching the "if honest scores were given" framing this diagnostic is meant to test.

    A "betrayal" is a sign disagreement (both nonzero) between the noisy and honest upsets: the
    runoff would have gone the other way if these SAME voters had cast honest ballots instead.
    voter_corruption_rate is the more granular input signal: among voters with a genuine (nonzero)
    honest-ballot preference for the pair, the fraction whose ACTUAL ballot disagrees in sign.
    """
    score0to = Score(topRank, True)
    n_betrayals = n_decisive = n_voter_corrupt = n_voter_decisive = n_harm = 0
    vse_harm_total = 0.0
    for i in range(niter):
        true_electorate = electorates[i] if electorates is not None else MODEL(NVOT, NCAND)
        perceived = make_perceived_electorate(true_electorate, epistemic_t)
        ballot_electorate, _ = apply_participation_friction(perceived, true_electorate, awareness_l, fatigue_l)  # Score-only helper, never feeds Irv
        ballots = [score0to.honBallot(score0to, voter, None) for voter in ballot_electorate]
        honest_ballots = [score0to.honBallot(score0to, voter, None) for voter in true_electorate]
        baseResults = list(map(score0to.candScore, zip(*ballots, strict=False)))
        (runnerUp, top) = sorted(range(len(baseResults)), key=lambda i: baseResults[i])[-2:]

        noisy_upset = sum(_sign4(b[runnerUp] - b[top]) for b in ballots)
        honest_upset = sum(_sign4(hb[runnerUp] - hb[top]) for hb in honest_ballots)

        if noisy_upset != 0 and honest_upset != 0:
            n_decisive += 1
            if _sign4(noisy_upset) != _sign4(honest_upset):
                n_betrayals += 1
                utils = true_electorate.socUtils
                best, rand = max(utils), mean(utils)
                actual_winner = runnerUp if noisy_upset > 0 else top
                honest_winner = runnerUp if honest_upset > 0 else top
                if actual_winner != honest_winner:
                    vse_harm_total += (normalized_vse(utils[honest_winner], best, rand)
                                        - normalized_vse(utils[actual_winner], best, rand))
                    n_harm += 1

        for b, hb in zip(ballots, honest_ballots):
            honest_sign = _sign4(hb[runnerUp] - hb[top])
            if honest_sign != 0:
                n_voter_decisive += 1
                if _sign4(b[runnerUp] - b[top]) != honest_sign:
                    n_voter_corrupt += 1

    return dict(
        betrayal_rate=(n_betrayals / n_decisive if n_decisive else float("nan")),
        n_decisive=n_decisive, n_betrayals=n_betrayals,
        voter_corruption_rate=(n_voter_corrupt / n_voter_decisive if n_voter_decisive else float("nan")),
        avg_vse_harm=(vse_harm_total / n_harm if n_harm else 0.0), n_harm=n_harm,
    )

def _betrayal_table(stats_by_key, key_header, key_fmt=str):
    header = [key_header, "Betrayal rate", "Voter corruption rate", "Avg VSE harm when betrayed", "n decisive"]
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(header)]
    for key, stats in stats_by_key.items():
        lines.append("| " + " | ".join([
            key_fmt(key),
            f"{stats['betrayal_rate'] * 100:.1f}%" if stats["n_decisive"] else "n/a",
            f"{stats['voter_corruption_rate'] * 100:.2f}%",
            f"{stats['avg_vse_harm'] * 100:.1f} pts" if stats["n_harm"] else "0.0 pts",
            str(stats["n_decisive"]),
        ]) + " |")
    display(Markdown("\n".join(lines)))

_betrayal_table(betrayal_by_epistemic_t, "epistemic_t", key_fmt=lambda t: f"{t:.2f}")

Reading this table: betrayal_rate is the fraction of elections where the runoff pair had a genuine (nonzero) HONEST-ballot preference AND the actual, corrupted ballots' pairwise sign disagreed with it -- i.e., the runoff mechanically produced the outcome the SAME voters' honest ballots would have rejected (honest ballots, not raw utilities, so this isolates noise/friction from STAR's own separate 0..5 discretization loss -- see the note above). voter_corruption_rate is the more granular, noisier input signal: the fraction of individual voters (among those with a real honest-ballot preference on the pair) whose actual ballot disagreed. avg_vse_harm is the VSE cost, in percentage points, specifically attributable to betrayed elections. At the "Ideal" scenario (epistemic_t=awareness_l=fatigue_l=1.0) both rates should be exactly zero (or n/a if no election produced a decisive pair) -- ballots then exactly reflect true utilities, so no disagreement is possible; this is the sanity check for the whole diagnostic.

Observed: both rates are exactly 0.0% at "Ideal" and at epistemic_t=1.00, confirming the diagnostic itself is sound -- with zero noise/friction, the runoff never disagrees with what honest ballots would have decided. From there the betrayal rate climbs steeply and close to monotonically as conditions degrade: 0% -> 36% -> 40.5% -> 47.3% across Ideal -> Mild -> Moderate -> Heavy friction, and 0% -> 25.6% -> 30.1% -> 34.5% -> 40% -> 48.5% as epistemic_t alone falls from 1.0 to 0.0. Nearly half of all elections with a genuine honest preference on the runoff pair get that preference overturned by noise/friction alone once conditions are bad enough -- and the average VSE harm in those betrayed elections is large (roughly 13-119 points, growing with adversity), confirming this isn't just a frequent but low-stakes flip: when the runoff gets corrupted, it tends to matter.
